report.summary: (model supplied no summary; its answer is preserved in handoff)

handoff.purpose: Normalize turns, refuse with receipts, chain records to the transcript store.

symbols.name: _scan_roster
symbols.note: Scans participant texts for secret-floor rule hits; returns first hit or None.

symbols.name: _reject_unknown
symbols.note: Raises ValueError on any key not in the allowed set; refuses to drop caller data silently.

symbols.name: _norm_evidence
symbols.note: Validates evidence items as exactly {'path','sha256'}, lowercases sha, normalizes path slashes, returns sorted list.

symbols.name: _norm_strs
symbols.note: Returns sorted, deduped list of non-empty stringified values.

symbols.name: _norm_meta
symbols.note: Rejects unknown meta keys; fills defaults for cli_version, endpoint, transport; passes through numeric fields.

symbols.name: _norm_class
symbols.note: Requires independence_class dict with exactly {'vendor','family'}; returns those as strings.

symbols.name: _normalize_turn
symbols.note: Fills the dcouncil/1 turn envelope with fail-closed validation of actor, status, content, reason.

symbols.name: _refusal_receipt
symbols.note: Builds a stand-in refused turn carrying only the rule label; optionally anonymizes identity fields.

symbols.name: _file_sig
symbols.note: Returns (size, mtime_ns) of store file or None if missing.

symbols.name: _chain_state
symbols.note: Returns cached tail entry_sha, record count, turn count; reloads when file signature changes.

symbols.name: _ends_without_newline
symbols.note: Checks whether the store file's last byte is not a newline.

symbols.name: _write_anchor
symbols.note: Writes the anchor JSON file with council_id, count, head, ts.

symbols.name: _chain_records
symbols.note: Chains a pre-ordered batch, assigns seq to turns, appends lines to store and returns ids.

claims.text: Every free-text and every path channel of a turn. Returns the rule label that fired (a fixed string -- NEVER matched text), or None.
claims.why: The docstring describes _scan_turn, whose body is above this chunk; this chunk contains only _scan_roster. The claim about returning a fixed label cannot be verified here.

claims.text: withheld: content channel ONLY (see the carve-out in the module docstring).
claims.why: The comment is in _scan_turn, whose body is above this chunk; this chunk cannot observe whether withheld is treated as content-only.

claims.text: Independence is a property of WEIGHTS, not of endpoints: local qwen2.5-coder:7b and bench qwen2.5-coder:7b are one voice on two sockets. The class is (vendor, model family) and is mandatory.
claims.why: _norm_class requires the dict to have exactly {'vendor','family'} and raises otherwise, making the class mandatory and defined by vendor/family, not host/endpoint.

claims.text: Fill the dcouncil/1 turn envelope, fail-closed. Absence is REPORTED, never guessed favourably.
claims.why: The function raises on invalid actor, status, reason, content length; records 'unknown' for missing model/lane rather than inferring; rejects unknown keys via _reject_unknown.

claims.text: status='refused' is MINTED by the secret floor, never asserted by a caller: a caller-authored refusal is an unverified claim that a scan happened
claims.why: The code raises ValueError for any caller-supplied status 'refused', so only the secret floor can produce it.

claims.text: an empty 'spoke' turn is a silent degrade -- record status='unavailable' with a machine reason instead
claims.why: The code raises if content is blank for status 'spoke', forcing the caller to use 'unavailable' with a reason instead.
The code raises if status is 'spoke' and reason is not None.

claims.text: unavailable needs a machine reason from UNAVAILABLE_REASONS!, got ...
claims.why: The code raises if status is 'unavailable' and reason is not in UNAVAILABLE_REASONS.

claims.text: anomaly needs a reason from ANOMALY_REASONS!
claims.why: The code raises if status is 'anomaly' and reason is not in ANOMALY_REASONS.

claims.text: A refused turn's stand-in. Carries the rule LABEL only -- never the matched text, never the content, never the evidence paths (the offending path is often the secret).
claims.why: The receipt sets content to '', refs to [], evidence to [], withheld to [], and reason to the rule label; no matched text or evidence paths are carried.

claims.text: anonymous drops even the identity fields, for when the identity itself tripped the floor.
claims.why: When anonymous is True, actor/vendor/model/independence_class/role/lane are replaced with redacted or defaults; meta is normalized with None, dropping transport and latency.

claims.text: Tail entry_sha + record/turn counts, cached and invalidated by file signature. MUST be called under _WRITE_LOCK. Any cross-process append changes the size, forcing a reload, so a stale prev can never be bound.
claims.why: The function caches by resolved path and file signature; if signature differs it reloads via load_transcript and recomputes tail/count/turns. The lock requirement is stated but not enforced here; the caller _chain_records holds _WRITE_LOCK.

claims.text: Chain a pre-ORDERED batch and append it. One chain timestamp for the whole batch: ts is inside entry_sha, so per-turn wall clock would make the head depend on completion order.
claims.why: A single ts is computed once (ts = ts or _now_iso()) and used for every record in the batch; entry_sha is derived from that same ts.

claims.text: Read-then-write happens inside the lock so a concurrent append can neither tear a line nor bind two lines to one prev.
claims.why: The entire read (via _chain_state) and write (store_path.open('a')) occur inside the with _WRITE_LOCK block.

claims.text: A torn (newline-less) tail is separated with a leading newline so this batch lands as its own parseable lines instead of fusing onto the fragment and being destroyed while the caller holds a success id.
claims.why: The code checks _ends_without_newline(store_path) and prepends '\n' to the batch before writing; this separates the batch from a fragment.

claims.text: unknown is recorded, never omitted and never inferred.
claims.why: model defaults to 'unknown' when missing or empty; lane defaults to 'untrusted' (not 'unknown' but a fixed value), and vendor defaults to actor.split('.')[1] which is an inference; however the comment specifically targets model, and model is recorded as 'unknown'.

claims.text: Paths an egress lane declined to send. Named, not counted.
claims.why: withheld is normalized via _norm_strs into a list; no counting or aggregation is performed.

claims.text: untrusted by default: deciding a vendor is trusted with this repo's IP is a policy decision, and a default argument must not make it.
claims.why: lane defaults to 'untrusted' when missing or empty; a caller must explicitly provide a lane to override the default.

claims.text: Numeric accounting survives a refusal (it cannot carry a credential); the free-text meta strings do not.
claims.why: When not anonymous, the receipt keeps latency_ms (numeric) from meta but drops cli_version, endpoint, started_ts, prompt_tokens, completion_tokens, cost_usd, transport is kept as 'unknown' if missing; free-text strings like cli_version/endpoint are dropped.

observations.what: _chain_records assigns seq to turns inside the lock but does not persist the updated seq to the store before computing body_sha; however body_sha is computed after seq assignment, and the record written includes seq, so the chain is consistent.

_refusal_receipt when anonymous drops all identity fields but still keeps 'blind', 'self_review', 'duplicate_class' flags from the original turn; these flags might reveal identity indirectly (e.g., self_review implies the actor was the reviewer).

_chain_records writes a trailing newline after each batch, and _ends_without_newline checks for a missing newline; however if the store file is empty (size 0), _ends_without_newline returns False, so no leading newline is added; the batch is written as the first line, which is correct.

_normalize_turn derives vendor from actor.split('.')[1] when vendor is missing; this could fail if actor has fewer than two dots, but actor is validated by _ACTOR_RE which presumably enforces a pattern with at least two dots.
_norm_evidence sorts by (path, sha256), which is deterministic but may change the order of evidence items relative to the caller's intent; the docstring does not claim to preserve order.

_chain_state caches by resolved path and file signature; if the file is deleted and recreated with the same size and mtime (unlikely but possible), the cache would be stale; the signature includes mtime_ns which reduces this risk.

risks: _refusal_receipt | medium | anonymous receipt retains blind/self_review/duplicate_class flags which may leak identity | check whether those flags are cleared when anonymous is True

_normalize_turn | medium | vendor derived from actor.split('.')[1] assumes actor has at least two dots; _ACTOR_RE likely enforces that, but if not, IndexError | verify _ACTOR_RE pattern in another chunk

_chain_records | low | seq assigned but not persisted before body_sha; however body_sha computed after assignment and record written includes seq, so chain is consistent | confirm body_sha does not include seq in a way that breaks integrity
_chain_state | low | file signature may not detect a delete-and-recreate with identical size/mtime | consider adding inode or ctime to signature
_norm_evidence | low | sorting evidence changes caller order; deterministic but may surprise callers expecting original order | document or preserve order if order is semantically meaningful
